question.text: A newly-launched Cat III AIF, Aravalli Long-Short Fund, had its First Close on 1-August 2024. On what date (earliest) must it start reporting data to the benchmarking agency under SEBI's framework?

answer.text: After completing one year from First Close, i.e., from 1-Aug-2025 onwards (reporting from the next half-yearly date, 30-Sep-2025)
After three years from First Close, i.e., 1-Aug-2027

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI operational guideline (Box 8.6, Section A, para (b)): 'AIFs/Schemes that have completed at least one year from First Close, shall provide all the necessary information/data to the Benchmarking Agencies.' First Close 1-Aug-2024 → one year completed on 1-Aug-2025 → first reporting date is the next half-yearly cut-off, i.e., 30-Sep-2025. The Trap: Option A and B jump the gun — SEBI requires at least one year of fund history before peer comparability. Option D (3 years) confuses with PE/VC vintage-year reporting conventions, not Cat III. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C / XIX-D test the same 1-year-from-First-Close rule. This is a common XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) question framed from the investor-disclosure side. Manager's Pro-Tip: Use the one-year runway to set up clean NAV-strike discipline, audit trails, and valuation-agency agreements so that the first submission to the benchmarking agency is defensible. Messy early data becomes your permanent benchmark history — fix it before reporting starts.
